observed.description: What was observed in tmux afterwards, for example the new pane id.

reason.description: Why it failed or why the outcome is unknown.

snapshot.description: Engine snapshot; peers share the build family checked at handshake.

DaemonEvent.description: One entry of the daemon's event log: metadata only, never terminal content.

host.description: The remote host the event is about, if any.

kind.description: tmux.topology, actions.outcome, hosts.state, or apps.registered (see docs/events.md).

pane.description: The pane the event is about, if any.

sequence.description: Increases by one per event within a daemon instance, from 1.

state.description: An action outcome or a host's link state.

subject.description: An action id or launch id.

clients.description: Connected API clients, including the caller.

Decoration.description: A mark on one line of a pane: data for clients to draw, never part of the terminal stream.

cols.description: The pane's width when marked; a reflow invalidates it.

row.description: The line's row counted from the top of the pane's history.

text.description: The line, as it was when marked.

decorations.description: Still valid: same generation and width, and the line is still at its row.

EndpointStatus.description: One tmux server the daemon manages.

detail.description: Why the link is not live.

socket.description: tmux -L name or -S path, as configured.

EventBatch.description: Pushed as `events.batch`: a gap, if any, comes before the events.

cursor.description: Resume after this sequence to continue where this batch ends.

EventGap.description: Events in first..=last were not delivered; re-read state that depends on them.

after.description: Resume after this sequence; without it, only new events follow.

instance.description: The daemon instance the cursor came from (EventSubscription.instance).

kinds.description: Kinds or kind prefixes (`actions` matches `actions.outcome`); empty means every kind.

panes.description: Only events about these panes; empty means every event.

quota.description: How many events this subscriber may fall behind before it skips ahead with a gap; default 1024.

instance.description: This daemon instance; cursors are valid only within it.

oldest.description: The oldest sequence the log still keeps.

config_error.description: Why extensions.yaml could not be read; nothing was started from it.

failures.description: Consecutive failures; reset after a minute of running.

restarts.description: Times it was started again since the daemon started.

version.description: What it said in its extension.hello answer.

FilterInput.description: A typed trigger: fixed text typed into a pane. Matched text is never typed.

badge.description: The badge text for decorate: badge.

breaker.description: Triggers (topic, recipient, input) allowed in any 10 s; one more trips the filter. Default 50.

decorate.description: Mark each matched line on its pane (drawn by clients).

event.description: Record each match as a filters.matched event (scripts receive them with on_event).

grant.description: What the filter may do: taps.subscribe for its panes, plus what its outputs need.

input.description: Type this into a pane on each match.

name.description: Unique; its sender identity is filter:<name>.

pattern.description: As in terminal.query: a regular expression, or plain text with `literal`.

per_second.description: Matches acted on per second; more are counted as dropped. Default 20.

recipient.description: Send each matched line to this instance.

topic.description: Publish each matched line here (the derived stream).

reason.description: Why it is paused or tripped.

skipped_own.description: Lines skipped because they echo this filter's own input.

FocusInput.description: Sent to the application only if it asked for focus reports.

Grant.description: What a connection may do. The user's own clients hold the owner grant (everything). A narrow grant lists its methods (exact names, or `service.*`), the panes it may read, follow, or type into, and an optional expiry. Checked by the daemon before every request; data can never widen it.

owner.description: Everything is allowed (the user's own clients).

panes.description: Panes in scope; requests naming another pane are refused.

HostCall.description: One typed call forwarded to a connected host's daemon: `payload` is the method's parameters as Protobuf, exactly as in a local call. Methods that stream (subscriptions and watches) are refused.

HostConnect.description: Connect the local daemon (the coordinator) to the daemon on another host through system ssh, running `dream bridge --stdio` there. SSH configuration, keys, and host verification stay the user's.

auto_reconnect.description: Retry a dropped connection by itself; default: the profile's policy, or off for a host given here.

destination.description: SSH destination: host alias, user@host, or ssh:// URI.

dream.description: Remote dream executable; default `dream` on the remote PATH. A leading ~/ is the remote home.

name.description: A local label for this host; unique among hosts.

tmux.description: Remote tmux executable, for a remote daemon that has to be started.

HostFailure.description: Why the last attempt failed, and so whether retrying can help.

HostList.description: Every profile in hosts.yaml and every other host connected since the daemon started.

profiles_error.description: hosts.yaml exists but is invalid: the error, with its location.

HostReply.description: The remote daemon's result for a HostCall, as Protobuf.

attempts.description: Failed attempts since the last live connection.

detail.description: Why the host is not live: the reason and SSH's last diagnostic lines.

last_contact_unix_ms.description: Last successful exchange with the remote daemon.

next_retry_unix_ms.description: When the next automatic attempt starts, if one is scheduled.

remote.description: The remote daemon's protocol and build, once live.

remote_instance.description: Changes when the remote daemon restarts.

HostSubscribe.description: Follow a pane on a connected host through this daemon: the reply and the `terminal.*` events are those of terminal.subscribe, with this connection's own subscription id. When SSH drops and the host comes back, the subscription resumes from the host's journal by itself; it ends with host_lost or host_restarted when it cannot.

bytes.description: Encoded bytes delivered to the pane.

plan_id.description: The id of the reviewed plan; a different plan now is refused.

InstallPlan.description: What hosts.install would do, for review: found by probing the host through SSH. Installing requires this plan's id, so nothing different from what was reviewed can be installed.

installed.description: The installed server's VERSION first line, if any.

steps.description: Each change, in order, in plain words.

target.description: The matching Rust target, such as x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.

version.description: The version that would be installed (this daemon's own).

artifacts.description: Directory of server archives on this machine; default DREAMER_SERVER_ARTIFACTS, else share/dreamer/server beside this daemon.

check.description: What the installed dream --version printed on the host.

remote_dream.description: The installed dream, as run on the host.

artifacts.description: The directory the job was given as DREAMER_JOB_ARTIFACTS.

pane.description: Its tmux pane: read its output with terminal.read while the pane remains.

argv.description: The exact program and arguments; no shell.

env.description: Added to the job's environment; names are [A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*.

name.description: The tmux window name; default the program's name.

session.description: The session for its window; default the first session.

KeyInput.description: A key press, encoded by the daemon with the pane's current keyboard modes.

held.description: An auto-repeat of a key held down.

key.description: W3C KeyboardEvent.code name: KeyA, Digit1, ArrowUp, Enter, F5, ...

text.description: The text the key produced on the client keyboard layout.

LaunchApp.description: Start a program in a new tmux window as a registered app. The daemon writes a single-use ticket to an owner-only file and gives the program only that file's path (DREAMER_LAUNCH_TICKET) and the launch id (DREAMER_LAUNCH_ID). The program registers with them for `grant`.

argv.description: Exact program and arguments; never a shell string.

grant.description: What the app may do; with no panes and not all_panes, its own pane.

name.description: The window name; default the app id.

ttl_ms.description: How long the ticket is valid; default 60000.

missed.description: Messages dropped for this subscription since the previous delivery, because it was full.

cause.description: The message this one answers or was caused by.

claimed_sender.description: What the sender said about itself: a claim, never authority.

id.description: Assigned by the daemon; increases per message.

origin.description: The first message of this causal chain (its own id when it starts one).

recipient.description: The instance a direct message, request, or reply is for.

request.description: A request: answer it with messages.reply.

schema.description: The payload's schema version, chosen by the sender.

MessagePublish.description: A topic message or a direct message: give exactly one of topic and recipient.

sender.description: A claimed sender; recipients see it as claimed_sender, next to the stamped one.

topic.description: Not dreamer.*, human.*, policy.*, or approval.*: those are the daemon's.

MessageSender.description: Who sent a message, stamped by the daemon from the connection; never taken from the sender.

instance.description: A registered app's instance, or owner:<n> for one of the user's own clients.

topics.description: Exact topics, service.* prefixes, or *. Direct messages and requests to this connection arrive regardless.

instance.description: This connection's identity as a recipient.

cwd.description: Latest working directory the program reported (OSC 7).

journal_first_sequence.description: Oldest retained journal record; sequence + 1 when none is retained.

reattaches.description: Times the mirror was rebuilt from a fresh capture because the pane's output outran it.

MouseInput.description: A mouse event at a cell of the pane's canonical grid, encoded with the application's mouse tracking mode and format. Nothing is sent when the application does not track this kind of event. Wheel steps are presses of wheel_up or wheel_down, one per step.

buttons_held.description: A button is down (for drag reporting).

NewWindow.description: A window at the end of a session; it runs the default shell unless argv is given.

argv.description: Exact program and arguments; never a shell string.

generation.description: Process generation; changes when the pane is respawned.

mode.description: A tmux-drawn mode the pane is in (copy-mode, tree-mode, ...). Its screen is tmux's, not the program's, and Dreamer does not draw it.

PasteInput.description: Bracketed exactly once when the application enabled bracketed paste. A paste larger than one request is sent in parts with the same id and `more` set on all but the last; the daemon encodes the whole paste once (at most 64 MiB).

line.description: Index in the searched window, oldest first.

match_start.description: Byte offsets of the match in text.

notes.description: What was cut and why, and hosts that could not be searched.

truncated.description: A bound cut the answer short; see notes.

history.description: Scrollback lines to include before the screen; default 0, at most 10000.

effects.description: Live effects of these records; never present in replayed records.

ticket.description: The contents of the ticket file.

RpcError.description: A failed call. Codes follow JSON-RPC 2.0 where they apply.

ScriptLimits.description: Absent fields take the defaults (16 MiB, 50 ms, 5 s).

call_ms.description: Running time per call into the script.

events.description: Event kinds (prefixes) passed to the script's on_event; needs events.subscribe in the grant.

name.description: Unique among loaded scripts; its sender identity is script:<name>.

source.description: Luau source; it runs once on load, then its handlers are called.

errors.description: Handler errors (not budget overruns); the instance keeps running.

revision.description: The source revision running: 1 on load, +1 per successful reload.

SendInput.description: Exact bytes to whatever runs in the pane now. With `generation`, the input is refused if the pane's process was replaced.

SendKeys.description: Named keys (tmux key names such as Enter or C-c) to the pane.

effect.description: What stops and what keeps running (tmux panes always keep running).

applied.description: The size was sent to tmux.

owner.description: The asking client owns the window's size.

SizeWindow.description: Ask for a tmux window's size in cells. Applied only for the window's sizing owner: the first client to ask, until it disconnects or releases the window. Send it when your own window changes size, never in reaction to a topology change.

release.description: Give up ownership instead (cols and rows are ignored).

SplitPane.description: Split a pane; the new pane runs the default shell unless argv is given.

argv.description: Exact program and arguments; never a shell string.

idempotency_key.description: Resubmitting the same key returns the first action; different content is rejected.

checkpoint_pause_us.description: How long the snapshot held the pane's owner.

cwd.description: The pane's current working directory: state, not an event.

scrollback_lines.description: The mirror's scrollback limit; a replica uses the same so both keep the same history.

sequence.description: Checkpoint mode: the checkpoint's sequence. Replay mode: the resume point.

title.description: The pane's current title: state, not an event.

cols.description: text: the pane's width when the lines were read.

ended.description: The pane is gone; nothing more follows for it.

lines.description: text: lines that scrolled into history, oldest first.

meta.description: meta: the pane's state when it changed.

raw.description: raw: bytes as the program wrote them.

rows.description: text: each line's row, counted from the top of the pane's history at the time.

screen.description: text: rows of an alternate screen that changed.

TapGap.description: Output this tap did not deliver. The pane itself lost nothing.

reason.description: lagging (the tap fell behind), window (more lines scrolled between looks than a look reads), or restarted (the pane's program was replaced).

sequence.description: Records applied; it advancing means output.

row.description: 0 is the top row of the screen.

every_pane.description: Follow every mirrored pane, including later ones (needs all_panes).

interval_ms.description: How often text and meta taps look for changes; default 250, at least 50.

TerminalEffect.description: What applying one live record did besides changing the screen. Sent only to subscribers live when it happened: never replayed from the journal, a checkpoint, bootstrap, or a reconnect.

clipboard.description: Text the program wrote to the clipboard (OSC 52). Sent only to the subscription of the pane's focused client.

client.description: The sending client's id (as in TerminalSubscribe); focus events make it the pane's focused client.

generation.description: Refuse the input if the pane's process was replaced.

TerminalQuery.description: Which panes' recent lines match a pattern. Every bound is enforced; a truncated answer says so.

hosts.description: Connected hosts to search too (all their panes); `*` means every live host.

lines.description: How many of each pane's newest lines (screen included); default 200, at most 2000.

panes.description: The panes to search; empty means every mirrored pane (needs all_panes).

pattern.description: A regular expression (linear time, size-limited), or plain text with `literal`.

timeout_ms.description: Default 2000, at most 10000; panes not searched in time are reported.

title.description: Only panes whose title matches this regular expression.

TerminalRecord.description: One journaled change. A resize when cols and rows are set, otherwise output bytes.

client.description: An id the client picks once per window; it names the client in TerminalInput too, so the daemon can address effects such as clipboard writes to exactly one.

resume_epoch.description: With generation and sequence: continue after this record instead of a new checkpoint, if it is still retained.

TerminalText.description: A pane's text as the daemon's canonical mirror holds it.

epoch.description: The control connection epoch the mirror belongs to.

lines.description: Oldest first: history lines, then the screen.

sequence.description: Records applied since the mirror attached.

TextInput.description: Committed text (typing or IME commit); never IME preedit.

Tier.description: Observation tier (spec 16.6). Hot: visible in a client. Warm: mirrored and journaled, not shown. Cold: metadata only.

incarnation.description: Identifies this run of the tmux server. Session, window, and pane ids are only meaningful within one incarnation: never reuse a saved id from another.

endpoint.description: Endpoint name; the default endpoint when absent.

TopologyUpdate.description: A topology with its revision. After tmux.watch, the connection gets one as a `tmux.topology` event whenever the topology changes (including changes another tmux client made), coalesced to the latest.

revision.description: Increases with every change; never repeats within a daemon run.

allow_older.description: Install even when the host has a newer version.

plan_id.description: The id of the reviewed install plan.

UpgradeResult.description: An upgrade is a restart of the host's daemon, not a handover: its tmux sessions and panes keep running, but views of them start again from fresh checkpoints.

from.description: The version installed before, if any.

restarted.description: The host's daemon was restarted on the new version.

build_family.description: Engine build family; peers must match exactly.

layout_supported.description: False for layouts Dreamer cannot draw yet (floating panes).

sessions.description: Sessions the window is linked into.
